channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em encontro com empresários, Simone Tebet fez revelações surpreendente sobre Lula
item.description: Simone Tebet revealed that the Ministry of Planning, under her leadership, completed a 25-year strategic plan for Brazil with targets across all sectors, but President Lula never signed the decree to implement it, citing discomfort in doing so during his final year in office. She also opposed closed-list proportional representation in political reform, arguing it would enable nepotism and that Brazil lacks the maturity for such a system.

item.title: Por que Brasil x Marrocos está entre os jogos mais procurados da Copa
item.description: The Brazil vs. Morocco match at the 2026 World Cup is among the most sought-after games, with 75,000 tickets sold in advance — behind only the final and the opening match. It leads in hospitality suite sales, surpassing even the final, showing fans now prioritize premium experiences over just watching the game.

item.title: Carlos diz que Jair Bolsonaro piorou: "Sonolência se prolongou"
item.description: Former councilman Carlos Bolsonaro stated that his father, Jair Bolsonaro, has experienced prolonged drowsiness due to stronger medications prescribed for worsening health conditions. He said that during a scheduled visit between 8 a.m. and 10 a.m., Bolsonaro remained asleep almost the entire time, waking only at 9:55 a.m., allowing just five minutes of interaction. Carlos criticized the visitation restrictions imposed by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, claiming they harm the former president’s health and prevent his granddaughters from attending Brazil’s 2026 World Cup opener with him.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro visita o pai em prisão domiciliar em Brasília
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro visited his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest at the Solar de Brasília condominium on Saturday morning (June 13), accompanied by his wife and two minor daughters. The visit was authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, who also ordered a prior inspection and banned cell phone use during the meeting. Jair Bolsonaro has been serving house arrest since March 27 for humanitarian reasons, with the term set to end on June 25, following his conviction for attempting a coup d'état.

item.title: Novo tenta consolidar candidatura de Zema, mas mantém pontes com PL nos estados
item.description: The New Party is positioning Romeu Zema’s gubernatorial candidacy as a right-wing alternative to Bolsonarism for the 2026 presidential race, while maintaining strategic alliances with the PL party at the state level to strengthen its congressional presence. The party aims to elect between 12 and 20 federal deputies, backed by a budget of up to R$90 million and gains from the 2024 municipal elections. Its strategy includes running full slates in most states and leveraging Zema’s potential national poll performance to boost proportional candidates nationwide.

item.title: Nunes Marques rejeita pedido para barrar filme sobre Bolsonaro durante eleições
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the TSE rejected a request by allies of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to block the screening of the film "Dark Horse", which focuses on former President Jair Bolsonaro, during the 2026 electoral period. The decision, published on Friday the 12th, found no legal basis to censor the film in the context of the election campaign.

item.title: Antes de ser revogada, 'taxa das blusinhas' rendeu mais de R$ 2 bilhões ao governo em 2026
item.description: The 'blusinhas tax', a 20% federal import tax on international parcels under US$ 50, was revoked in mid-May 2026 after collecting R$ 2.13 billion from January to mid-May, a 15.4% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Although the federal tax was abolished, states continue to levy ICMS on these imports at rates between 17% and 20%. The measure, initially supported by national industry and officials like Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, faced criticism from consumers for raising prices on low-cost goods and reducing the appeal of platforms such as Shein, Shopee, and AliExpress.

item.title: Uma ameaça persistente e silenciosa desafia a campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula regained polling momentum after a R$200+ billion benefits package, leading Flávio Bolsonaro by 10 points in the first round and 6 in the second, with improved government approval and gains among undecided voters. However, the persistent silent threat of rising living costs endangers his support: 44% believe the economy worsened over the past year and 69% report higher food prices, threatening his appeal among non-ideologically aligned voters. Lula’s 53% rejection rate remains high, and the risk of backlash over food inflation echoes what damaged Bolsonaro in 2022.

item.title: Militante de esquerda confirma ameaças de morte a candidato a governador do RS
item.description: Federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL-RS), pre-candidate for governor of Rio Grande do Sul, received death threats from a left-wing profile identified as Cleomar dos Santos, a bag store employee from Novo Hamburgo. The messages included explicit threats like 'I missed the chance to burst your head' and were politically motivated. After a legislative police investigation, the perpetrator confessed, expressed regret, and Zucco now receives round-the-clock security due to rising political violence in Brazil.

item.title: Cotada para Fazenda se licencia de empresa por campanha de Flávio
item.description: Economist Daniella Marques took a leave from Legend, a wealth management firm, to join Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential pre-campaign. She is being considered for the Ministry of Finance and is expected to help shape the government plan, engage with financial markets, and strengthen outreach to female voters. The move follows a communication team overhaul that saw Marcello Lopes replaced by Eduardo Fischer and Alexandre Oltramari.

item.title: Nunes Marques rejeita pedido para barrar filme sobre Bolsonaro durante período eleitoral
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the TSE rejected a request by Lula allies to ban the screening of 'Dark Horse', a Bolsonaro biopic, during the 2026 electoral period. The ruling cited lack of standing, as the petitioners are not running for national office like the subject of the film, Flávio Bolsonaro. The petition also demanded financial transparency, referencing reports that Flávio Bolsonaro sought $24 million in funding for the film.

item.title: Dez ‘Brasis’ para bancar o governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government faces criticism for promoting populist measures in Congress, such as reducing the workweek, labeled irresponsible and electorally motivated. The text denounces the hypocrisy of government officials who condemn 'electoral handouts' while supporting proposals with uncalculated economic impacts. The narrative suggests these actions aim solely to secure political support to sustain the government.

item.title: Em vídeo à seleção brasileira, Lula pede “raça” e “concentração”
item.description: President Lula urged the Brazilian national team to play with grit, will, commitment, and team spirit in the 2026 World Cup, emphasizing the players’ peripheral origins and urging them to rise after setbacks. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro also posted a video accusing the Lula government of trying to 'steal' Brazil’s flag, claiming he 'rescued' it from the trash and using the national symbol to rally political support.

item.title: Produtora de “Dark Horse” avalia adiar o lançamento do filme
item.description: Go Up Entertainment is considering delaying the release of the film 'Dark Horse,' about the life of Jair Bolsonaro, to avoid association with the 2026 elections, as advised by lawyer Ricardo Sayeg. The film had a declared investment of R$ 75 million, tied to a judicial investigation involving the ICB — an institute linked to the producer’s owner — accused of diverting funds from a São Paulo City Hall contract.

item.title: Petrobras e Pemex vão assinar acordo de cooperação em junho, diz Magda
item.description: Petrobras and Pemex will sign a memorandum of understanding in June to establish initial cooperation in exploration and production, refining, petrochemicals, and data sharing. The announcement was made by Petrobras president Magda Chambriard during the reinauguration of the company’s headquarters in Rio de Janeiro, following a meeting between Lula and Sheinbaum discussing a potential deepwater agreement.

item.title: Como pedido de Bolsonaro para anular trama golpista afetou demais condenados
item.description: The defense strategy of Jair Bolsonaro to annul his conviction for involvement in a coup plot was viewed with skepticism by lawyers of other convicted individuals, who fear the appeal could be used as a political tool in favorable moments, such as after the 2026 elections. The initiative faces significant legal hurdles, as it requires the judiciary to admit error in its own ruling — considered highly unlikely. Moreover, the current political climate, marked by heightened tensions and pressure on the STF, reduces the likelihood of an impartial review.

item.title: Lula pede que seleção jogue com ‘alma’ na estreia contra o Marrocos na Copa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva released a video urging the Brazilian national team to play with 'soul' in their World Cup opener against Morocco, emphasizing the importance of playing for the Brazilian people and youth. He addressed coach Carlo Ancelotti, praising his experience as a player and coach, and urged the team to persevere through setbacks, stressing that scoring goals is what truly matters. Lula also said Ancelotti could become a hero like Feola, Zagallo, and Felipão, stating that Brazil does not play the World Cup to lose, but to win.

item.title: Esquerda ou direita? Estudo inédito mostra quem domina as redes no Brasil
item.description: A study by Ativaweb Datalab reveals that the right dominates social media in Brazil, with X (9.4/10) and TikTok (9.0/10) as its strongest platforms, while the left balances the playing field on Instagram. The Digital Right scores 82.4 points versus 74.8 for the Digital Left, showing a significant advantage in virality and organic mobilization. The left’s main challenge is adapting its language to new content formats, as the 2026 election will be heavily influenced by algorithms and the ability to capture and retain public attention.

item.title: Julia Zanatta surge como cotada para vice do Flávio Bolsonaro nas Eleições 2026
item.description: Julia Zanatta, a state deputy from Paraná representing the Liberal Party (PL), is being discussed as a potential vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket for the 2026 elections. Her name has gained traction within Bolsonarist circles due to her close ties with former President Jair Bolsonaro and her conservative policy stance. A potential Bolsonaro-Zanatta ticket would aim to solidify support from evangelical and right-wing voters in Paraná and across Brazil.

item.title: PRD e Solidariedade confirmam apoio à reeleição de Tarcísio em SP
item.description: The PRD-Solidariedade federation confirmed its support for the re-election of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) in São Paulo, during a meeting in the state capital attended by Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB). The endorsement was described as crucial for the re-election campaign, with national federation president Ovasco Resende stating the party would be on the ticket and provide 'all necessary support'. The decision dashed hopes of former Santo André mayor Paulo Serra (PSDB), who had been negotiating with Solidariedade for a potential gubernatorial run.

item.title: Como recompensa a ‘sacríficio’, PT oferece ‘terreno na lua’ em eventual Lula 4
item.description: The PT is offering federal positions as a reward for leaders willing to run in high-risk candidacies in 2026 to strengthen Lula’s presidential ticket in key states. Despite promises of ministerial roles or other government posts, several figures — including Rodrigo Pacheco, Marina Silva, and Márcio França — have declined, opting instead for safer races like Senate bids. This resistance is hindering the formation of competitive slates in São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Goiás, and Espírito Santo.

item.title: Desgaste de Flávio não impulsiona outros nomes da oposição, diz diretor da Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro losing ground in the presidential race, yet his decline is not boosting other opposition figures. Director Felipe Nunes says this reflects a deadlock in Brazil's right and center-right.

item.title: Lula manda recado à seleção antes da estreia contra Marrocos: 'Joguem com a alma'; veja vídeo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sent a motivational message to the Brazilian national team ahead of their 2026 World Cup opener against Morocco, urging players to play with soul, determination, and clinical finishing. He also expressed confidence in head coach Carlo Ancelotti, emphasizing that the current squad’s value lies in its own merit, not in comparisons to past generations.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, a cópia malfeita do pai preso
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attempts to position himself as a moderate version of his father but is seen as a flawed copy, using symbols like bulletproof vests and visits to Jerusalem to evoke Bolsonarist narratives. His support among women is weak, with only 39% intending to vote for him versus 47.6% for Lula, while male support is more balanced. His candidacy struggles due to a lack of genuine connection with evangelical voters and the perception that his actions are performative and disconnected from reality.

item.title: Condomínio de Bolsonaro processa ex-assessor de Janones após ato com megafone
item.description: The Solar Brasília condominium filed a lawsuit against Bernardo Moreira Amado Barros, a former aide to federal deputy André Janones, after he entered the premises under the pretense of visiting a resident and conducted a megaphone protest near former President Jair Bolsonaro’s residence, uttering insults and creating a hostile environment, particularly for families with children. The administration claims he violated internal rules, changed clothing during his stay, and was confronted by security, remaining for about an hour before leaving. The condominium seeks to ban his access and impose a fine of R$ 50,000 if he violates the order.

item.title: O número que Lula espera ver no próximo relatório da ONU sobre a fome
item.description: The Lula government expects the upcoming UN hunger report to show a reduction in severe food insecurity to at least 1% of the population, following last year's drop below 2.5%, which removed Brazil from the UN Hunger Map. The Ministry of Social Development believes the results will strengthen Lula's social image in his third term and will be strategically used in the 2026 pre-election period to contrast with Bolsonaro's administration.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lança jingle e critica Lula por uso do verde e amarelo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) released a pre-campaign video on Friday night, featuring a sertanejo jingle titled 'Vem com Fé' that references the World Cup, launched one day before Brazil's match against Morocco. The video criticizes President Lula for allegedly exploiting the national colors green and yellow for political purposes, accusing the government of appropriating these symbols for electoral gain.

item.title: “O medo é algo importante na vida”
item.description: Anxiety and fear are described as common feelings among players before Brazil's debut in the 2026 World Cup, with examples from former players like Alexandre Pato and Edinho, as well as Pelé, who revealed he cried before the 1970 final. Coach Carlo Ancelotti states that fear is important for life and sports performance.

item.title: Com baque nas pesquisas e racha entre aliados, campanha de Flávio enfrenta momento difícil
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is struggling after revelations that he sought 134 million reais in financial aid from Daniel Vorcaro, linked to major bank fraud, and following Trump's decision to impose new tariffs on Brazilian exports. These events weakened his anti-corruption stance and allowed Lula to regain ground by emphasizing national sovereignty, widening his lead in polls. Furthermore, a rift within Bolsonaro's base has left key allies like Michelle Bolsonaro, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Nikolas Ferreira unwilling to fully support his campaign.

item.title: STF prepara terreno para atuar na eleição
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, unilaterally suspended an electoral poll showing declining voter intentions for Flávio Bolsonaro, triggering concern at the STF, where four ministers privately suggest the Court may need to intervene in electoral propaganda due to fears of inadequate fake news countermeasures and rising AI threats. The text also covers the PEC to lower the age of criminal responsibility, digital vulnerabilities in the Judiciary, cases involving Zambelli and Master, and the STF’s influence on budgetary and administrative matters.

item.title: Em alerta vermelho ao governo, TCU faz críticas contundentes à situação fiscal do país
item.description: The TCU approved the federal government's 2025 accounts but issued strong criticisms of the country's fiscal situation, citing overestimated revenues, billionaire deficits in state-owned enterprises, and spending outside the fiscal target calculation — a loophole allowing the government to increase spending without constraint. Despite the approval, ministers warned that public finances urgently need adjustment due to rising public debt and fiscal laxity, which will be a major challenge for the next president. The decision will be sent to Congress, where historical leniency toward incumbent governments exists, though the TCU has previously used similar fiscal irregularities to support impeachment proceedings, as in the Dilma Rousseff case.

item.title: Fundo Eleitoral vai repassar R$ 4,9 bi a 30 partidos para eleições 2026
item.description: The Electoral Fund will distribute R$ 4.9 billion among the 30 parties registered with the TSE for the 2026 elections, with funds allocated exclusively to campaign financing, as corporate donations are prohibited. The PL leads with R$ 881 million, followed by the PT (R$ 615 million) and União Brasil (R$ 526 million), which together account for nearly 40% of the total. Distribution is based on each party's congressional representation.

item.title: Tarcísio recebe apoio de PRD e Solidariedade
item.description: The PRD-Solidariedade federation announced its support for the re-election of São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas in a meeting at the Palácio dos Bandeirantes. The meeting was attended by the national president of Solidariedade, Paulinho da Força, the national president of PRD, Ovasco Resende, and the mayor of São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes.

item.title: Os 30 mil 'porta-vozes do Lula'
item.description: The 'Voice of Lula' platform, launched by the Workers' Party (PT) on Tuesday, gained 30,000 sign-ups in its first 24 hours. The initiative aims to mobilize Lula's supporters to act as public defenders of his image and policy agenda. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Ministro da Fazenda concede entrevista ao vivo ao JOTA na sexta-feira (19/6)
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan will give a live interview to JOTA on Friday, June 19th at 11h, discussing Brazil's economic conditions and the impact of global factors such as the Iran war, U.S. trade negotiations, and El Niño. The interview takes place at a critical moment, just before electoral restrictions limit government actions starting in the second half of the year.

item.title: Maristela Basso na Crusoé: Por que o Brasil passou a confiar tão pouco no eleitor?
item.description: The article questions the paradoxical distrust of the Brazilian electorate despite the sophistication and success of the country’s Electoral Justice system, which has reduced fraud, modernized procedures, and contributed to democratic stability. Although the system is internationally praised, there is growing public distrust in elections, possibly fueled by polarization and misinformation.

item.title: A crítica de Ronaldo Caiado às eleições brasileiras
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, governor of Goiás, harshly criticized the Brazilian elections of 2026, claiming the electoral process is compromised by misinformation and lack of transparency. He urged urgent reforms to the electoral system to ensure integrity and public trust, emphasizing the need for greater oversight and verifiable technology. Caiado positioned himself as a defender of democratic integrity without naming specific candidates.

item.title: Brasil aparece pouco em newsletter dos EUA sobre noticiário internacional
item.description: The U.S.-based Semafor Flagship newsletter mentioned Brazil in only 10 of over 100 daily editions from January to May 2026, reflecting limited international coverage. Mentions included Wagner Moura’s Oscar nomination, the invasive golden mussel in the Amazon, Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential pre-candidacy announcement, Embraer’s record order backlog, the overturning of Lula’s veto on the dosimetry bill, and a Lula-Trump meeting. Despite some topics gaining national traction, international attention remained sparse and often tied to U.S. interests or domestic political controversies.

item.title: Polarizaram a seleção brasileira
item.description: On the eve of Brazil's opening match against Morocco in the World Cup, political polarization intensified. The PT launched the campaign 'Lula plays for Brazil,' seeking to link support for the former president to the defense of national sovereignty during the tournament.

item.title: PT critica Tarcísio por free flow, mas governo Lula também adota modelo em rodoviais federais
item.description: The PT criticizes Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for the chaotic implementation of free-flow tolling in São Paulo, citing lack of transparency and communication to drivers. However, Tarcísio’s allies note that the model was expanded under President Lula’s administration on federal highways, with ANTT authorizing electronic tolling in seven concessions. The state government denies electoral motives, claiming a technical and gradual strategy, despite postponements and cancellations of toll gantries due to public complaints.

item.title: Veja a programação das melhores rodas de samba do Rio neste fim de semana de jogo do Brasil na Copa do Mundo
item.description: This weekend in Rio de Janeiro combines the broadcast of Brazil’s World Cup debut with a diverse schedule of samba circles, including free and paid performances across neighborhoods such as Realengo, Lapa, Centro and Penha. Highlights include Terreiro de Crioulo at Sesc Nova Iguaçu, Arlindinho das Antigas at Beco do Rato and Arena Senado with LED screens for watching the match, plus attractions like Mal de Raiz, Quintal da Magia and Samba D'Coroa.

item.title: Geração 'pós-penta' é a mais empolgada com a Copa do Mundo, mas queda de otimismo no Brasil liga alerta
item.description: The generation born after Brazil’s fifth World Cup win (2002) shows the highest optimism for a sixth title in 2026, yet confidence among Brazilians aged 16–24 has dropped sharply—from 63% in July 2022 to 35% in April 2026, per Datafolha. While individuals like Bernardo Durães and Alice Fernandes express hope, prolonged team underperformance and traumatic memories such as the 7–1 loss to Germany in 2014 have weakened collective faith, despite perceptions of increased commitment from the current squad.

item.title: Passado de glórias e histórico de craques do Brasil provocam fascínio nos motoristas de aplicativo em Los Angeles
item.description: The text describes how ride-share drivers in Los Angeles, many of whom are immigrants from the Global South, express deep admiration for the Brazilian national football team, particularly legends like Ronaldinho, Ronaldo, Rivaldo, and Kaká. This admiration extends beyond sports, touching on cultural ties such as the large Lebanese community in São Paulo, and becomes a meaningful point of human connection amidst LA’s chaotic traffic.

item.title: Após revés na COP30, Brasil flexibiliza 'mapa do caminho' para atrair apoio à redução do uso de combustíveis fósseis
item.description: Brazil signaled that its global 'roadmap' for phasing out fossil fuels will be flexible after its proposal was excluded from the COP30 final text due to resistance from petrostates like Saudi Arabia, India, and Russia. The Lula administration aims to formally present the roadmap at COP31 in Turkey, despite domestic delays and criticism that the setback undermines Lula's international credibility on climate leadership.

item.title: Presidente do PT diz que caso 'Dark Horse' pode ampliar impacto eleitoral sobre bolsonarismo
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva says the 'Dark Horse' case, involving Banco Master's financing of the film, could politically damage Bolsonaro's camp if investigations progress, citing the proven closeness between Flávio Bolsonaro and businessman Daniel Vorcaro. He believes Flávio may retain part of his base but argues this doesn't equate to national electoral strength, emphasizing that bolsonarism has social force but not necessarily the capacity to win broad national projects.

item.title: Decisão que liberou Zambelli na Itália fala em 'dupla condição' e falta de imparcialidade de Moraes; veja próximos passos
item.description: Italy's Court of Cassation denied the extradition of former deputy Carla Zambelli to Brazil, stating that Minister Alexandre de Moraes acted as 'victim, witness, and judge' in the case, creating a 'dual condition' that undermines impartiality. The ruling is based on the 1989 Brazil-Italy extradition treaty, which bars surrender when there are doubts about respect for minimum defense rights. Zambelli was sentenced to 10 years in prison by Brazil's STF for being the intellectual author of the invasion of the National Justice Council (CNJ) system, with support from hacker Walter Delgatti Neto.

item.title: Sem palanque, Flávio Bolsonaro enfrenta desafio na Bahia, e PL racha sobre apoio à campanha de ACM Neto
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces resistance within the Bahia PL due to the lack of formal support from ACM Neto, who has aligned with Ronaldo Caiado in the first round. A faction of the PL pushes for early support for Flávio given his struggle to build Northeastern slates, while another faction argues that right-wing backing for ACM Neto is not automatic and requires dialogue. The split highlights internal party conflict and an added challenge for the senator in a state where Lula and the PT dominate.

item.title: rascunho
item.description: Brazil debuts in the 2026 World Cup against Morocco after 18 days of preparation since the call-up, under Carlo Ancelotti, in a short cycle marked by CBF presidency changes and Neymar’s absence due to injury. Vinicius Junior is seen as the candidate to fill the void left by the star player, while Ancelotti aims to balance the pressure of historical favoritism with a realistic and prepared discourse, emphasizing fear as a natural component of the challenge.

item.title: Entre gatinho e leão, seleção brasileira estreia na Copa do Mundo contra Marrocos com Ancelotti como escudo
item.description: Brazil opens its 2026 World Cup campaign against Morocco under Carlo Ancelotti, following a turbulent preparation marked by injuries (including Neymar’s) and CBF instability. Without Neymar, Vinicius Junior is seen as his natural replacement, while Ancelotti attempts to ease pressure with a balanced tone of fear and confidence, acknowledging Brazil’s 24-year World Cup drought.

item.title: Perícia não esclarece uso de R$ 75 milhões em filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: A private forensic report from Go Up Entertainment fails to detail the use of R$ 75 million allocated to the film Dark Horse, about Jair Bolsonaro. Of this amount, R$ 54.2 million was spent in the U.S. and R$ 20.9 million in Brazil, with only the domestic production and filming phase specified. The defense claims the funds are of private origin, while the ICB is suspected of diverting public money from São Paulo City Hall to finance the project.
